newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KIA refuses to disclose size of portfolio.
newsitem.headline: KIA refuses to disclose size of portfolio.

text.p: Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), sticking to official policy, refused on Tuesday to disclose the size of its foreign portfolio -- estimated at around $40 billion by independent economists and bankers.

KIA Chief Ali al-Badr refused to say in an interview how big the portfolio was but economists said it was now valued at around $40 billion mainly due to a rise in the value of equities and some cash injections by the state which secured higher revenues than forecast with the increase in world oil prices in recent months.

The state's KIA, once a major international investor, saw its nest egg shrink to around $30 billion from over $100 billion after paying for the 1991 Gulf War against Iraq, reconstruction and financing budget deficits.
Official sources said KIA's new board was expected to be announced in the next few weeks, reconfirming Badr in his post for another four years.

The board is made up of four ex-officio members -- the ministers of oil and finance, the central bank governor and the under-secretary for the Ministry of Finance -- and five independent members, including Badr.
